name: list_applications
summary: List installed applications (from Spotlight's index of .app bundles). Optionally narrow to those whose name contains a substring.

params.name: name_contains
params.description: Case-insensitive substring to filter app names (e.g. 'safari'). Omit to list everything.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max apps to return (default 200, max 500).

name: search_applications
summary: Search installed applications by a name substring. A focused alternative to list_applications when you already know part of the name.

params.name: query
params.description: Case-insensitive substring to match app names (e.g. 'note').

params.name: limit
params.description: Max matches to return (default 50, max 500).

name: list_running_applications
summary: List applications currently running with a visible presence (foreground apps, not background daemons). Requires permission to control System Events.

name: open_application
summary: Launch an installed app by name (or front it if already running), e.g. 'Notes', 'Safari'. Runs immediately; if it wasn't running, undo quits it again. For a web address use open_website; for a file use open_file.

params.name: name
params.description: App name, e.g. 'Safari', 'Notes', 'Visual Studio Code'.

name: open_file
summary: Open a file, optionally in a specific app (e.g. a PNG in Preview). With 'app', the preview flags whether that app supports the type, and undo quits the app if it wasn't already running. Omit 'app' for the file's default app. STAGED either way.

params.name: file
params.description: Path to the file (leading ~ ok), e.g. '~/Downloads/Leah.png'.

params.name: app
params.description: App to open it with, e.g. 'Preview', 'TextEdit'. Omit for the file's default app.

name: open_website
summary: Open a website in a browser, e.g. 'open YouTube' -> 'youtube.com', or 'open YouTube on Chrome'. Use when the subject is a web address (vs open_application or open_file). Must be http/https; a bare domain is opened over https. Omit 'browser' for the default. STAGED.

params.name: url
params.description: Web address: a bare domain ('youtube.com'), host:port ('localhost:8080'), or full 'https://...'. Must be http/https — not a file path, 'tel:', 'mailto:', etc.

params.name: browser
params.description: Browser to open it in, e.g. 'Safari', 'Google Chrome', 'Firefox'. Omit for the system default browser.

name: focus_application
summary: Bring an already-running (or launchable) app to the front and give it focus. Runs immediately; cannot be undone. Requires permission to control the target app.

params.name: name
params.description: App name to bring to the front, e.g. 'Safari'.

name: quit_application
summary: Quit a running application. STAGED — unsaved work could be lost and relaunching isn't a true reversal. Requires permission to control the target app.

params.name: name
params.description: App name to quit, e.g. 'Safari'.

name: search_app_store
summary: Search the Mac App Store for apps by name (e.g. 'Slack', 'Xcode'), returning each match's name, seller, price, and App Store id. Use this for 'download/install X': FIRST check search_applications (is it already installed?), then search_app_store; open a result's page with open_app_store_page (pass its id). If the app isn't on the App Store, fall back to open_website to the vendor's download page. Needs an internet connection.

params.name: query
params.description: App name to search for, e.g. 'Slack', 'Microsoft Word'.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max results to return (default 10, max 25).

name: open_app_store_page
summary: Open a specific app's page in the App Store app, given its numeric App Store id (from search_app_store). Runs immediately and just opens a window; installing or purchasing stays the user's click — it is never automated. For a plain web address use open_website instead.

params.name: track_id
params.description: The app's numeric App Store id, e.g. 803453959 (taken from a search_app_store result).

name: list_windows
summary: List the on-screen windows of foreground apps (title, top-left position, and size in pixels). Omit 'app' for every app's windows, or pass an app name to narrow to one. Uses System Events, so it needs Accessibility (and Automation) access.

params.name: app
params.description: App (process) name to narrow to, e.g. 'Safari'. Omit to list windows of every foreground app.

name: move_window
summary: Move an app's window to a new top-left screen position (x, y in pixels). Runs immediately; undo moves it back to where it was. Targets the front window by default, or pass 'window_index' (1 = frontmost). Uses System Events, so on first use macOS asks for BOTH Accessibility and Automation access.

params.name: app
params.description: App (process) name whose window to move, e.g. 'Safari'.

params.name: x
params.description: New left edge in screen pixels (0 = left of the main display; may be negative on a multi-monitor setup).

params.name: y
params.description: New top edge in screen pixels (0 = top of the main display).

params.name: window_index
params.description: Which window (1 = frontmost, 2 = next, ...). Defaults to the front window.

name: resize_window
summary: Resize an app's window to a new width and height in pixels. Runs immediately; undo restores the prior size. Targets the front window by default, or pass 'window_index' (1 = frontmost). Uses System Events, so on first use macOS asks for BOTH Accessibility and Automation access.

params.name: app
params.description: App (process) name whose window to resize, e.g. 'Safari'.

params.name: width
params.description: New window width in pixels (must be at least 1).

params.name: height
params.description: New window height in pixels (must be at least 1).

params.name: window_index
params.description: Which window (1 = frontmost, 2 = next, ...). Defaults to the front window.

name: minimize_window
summary: Minimize an app's window to the Dock. Runs immediately; undo un-minimizes it (only when it was not already minimized). Targets the front window by default, or pass 'window_index' (1 = frontmost). Uses System Events, so on first use macOS asks for BOTH Accessibility and Automation access.

params.name: app
params.description: App (process) name whose window to minimize, e.g. 'Safari'.

params.name: window_index
params.description: Which window (1 = frontmost, 2 = next, ...). Defaults to the front window.
